figure1: Figure 1. Conceptual retry-semantics model. The same ambiguous tool response is compatible with H0 (the original mutation did not execute) or H1 (it executed but acknowledgement was lost). Each hidden world is studied under Exact Replay and LLM Regeneration. Terminal state is classified as correct, missing, duplicate, or wrong/unintended effect; state that cannot be certified remains non-evaluable. Diagram arrows denote experimental branches, not transition probabilities. Regeneration can inspect state but is not guaranteed to do so.
figure2: Figure 2. Four-arm matched family. A single eligible original call M and task context are frozen across H0 Replay, H0 Regeneration, H1 Replay, and H1 Regeneration, each with an isolated arm scope. Within-world comparisons require both policies to be evaluable. The family interaction compares the two within-world policy differences and requires all four arms; a missing arm is never imputed.
figure3: Figure 3. Main external paired effects. Points show Replay-minus-Regeneration state-correctness differences in percentage points; whiskers show approved 95% paired Newcombe Method 10 intervals. Positive values favor Replay and negative values favor Regeneration. GitHub uses 63 matched H0 and 64 matched H1 families; the separately authorized Sheets post-incident replication uses 64 in H0 and 64 in H1. All estimates and intervals are secondary descriptive. Sheets is POST_INCIDENT_REPLICATION_NOT_PRIMARY_REPLACEMENT. Source-segment comparisons are disclosed in Table A1.
figure4: Figure 4. Policy correctness by provider and hidden world. Open circles (Replay) and filled squares (Regeneration) show observed correctness in the same matched population within each world; fractions are printed beside the markers. GitHub H0/H1 use 63/64 matched families; Sheets H0/H1 use 64/64. Provider panels are separate. No marginal correctness intervals were estimated. The complete GitHub H1 matched population and the completed Sheets replication show systematic H1 Replay duplication and successful H1 Regeneration under these controlled constructions.
figure5: Figure 5. External state-defect patterns and evaluability. Cells give counts, not rates, among recorded canonical arms; the evaluable denominator is printed per row. Missing, duplicate and wrong defects come from exact frozen evaluator tokens. GitHub H0 Regeneration has 4 missing effects; 3 enter the matched comparison because the remaining missing-effect arm has a non-evaluable Replay partner. The non-evaluable column is outside behavioral defect counts. One missing-effect arm also recorded HTTP 504. State-defect indicators are not assumed exclusive.
figureS1: Figure S1. Separate Razorpay stopped-run sequence. Each separately authorized allocation scheduled 256 arms and stopped after its own observed prefix. Boxes show evaluated, success, failure and unrun counts; they are not plotted as comparable provider-wide rates. Every stop is backed by raw HTTP 429 during GET Fetch All; the original historical ValueError wrapper is preserved. All recorded state failures are DUPLICATE_EFFECT, distinct from the provider stops. Sequence arrows denote governance history, not a randomized pacing or host intervention.
